name_note: In GTDB R232 this genus also holds genomes that NCBI names Gardnerella, so it is broader than the classical genus Bifidobacterium.

sentences.text: Bifidobacterium is a genus of anaerobic bacteria that are among the first microbes to colonise the human gastrointestinal tract.
They occupy niches connected directly or indirectly to the animal gut, including the human oral cavity, and specialise in carbohydrates that escape digestion higher in the intestine.
Bifidobacterium longum subspecies infantis is described as unusually able to consume human milk oligosaccharides, which shape the breastfed infant's intestinal community.
Reported functions include degrading non-digestible carbohydrates, producing B vitamins and protecting against infectious disease, a protection studied in mice colonised with bifidobacterial strains.
One study reports these milk-adapted bacteria are now rare in modern societies and that their absence early in life has been associated with systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation.
